title: Ansel and the Atlas
premise: Sable Pemberton, a courier for a collapsing republic, carries coded dispatches through occupied territory, trusting her invisibility to keep her alive. When a stranger leaves a child at her safehouse door with the words 'forget this face,' Sable's careful anonymity begins to unravel, forcing her to claim a family she never wanted and never admitted she needed. As the republic's final evacuation ship prepares to depart, her estranged sister arrives seeking passage, and the coded orders she carries reveal only one berth remains. Sable must decide whether duty to the dying state outweighs love for the living—and in the end, she burns the codes, gives the berth to the child, and stays behind, discovering that survival was never the same thing as living.
about_author: August Ashgrove is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing the letters of wartime evacuees. Their novels explore the quiet mathematics of sacrifice—what we count, what we carry, and what we leave behind.

chapters.title: The Weight of Paper
chapters.summary: Sable crosses a frozen border checkpoint with dispatches sewn into her coat hem, narrating her philosophy of carrying only what can be abandoned. POV: Sable. Emotional beat: controlled detachment established as armor.

chapters.title: Instructions in a Dead Language
chapters.summary: At the safehouse, Sable decodes her latest orders and learns the republic's capital has fallen; her mission is now evacuation logistics. POV: Sable. Emotional beat: the first crack in her certainty—orders now describe an ending.

chapters.title: The Child at the Door
chapters.summary: A stranger leaves a mute boy, Tomas, on the safehouse step with a note: forget this face. Sable, trained to notice everything, cannot stop cataloguing him. POV: Sable. Emotional beat: reluctant responsibility, fear of attachment.

chapters.title: What the Landlady Saw
chapters.summary: The safehouse landlady, Marta, quietly provides for Tomas, forcing Sable to confront how visible her 'invisibility' has always been. POV: Marta. Emotional beat: warmth that feels like exposure.

chapters.title: Cargo Manifest
chapters.summary: Sable travels to the port city and secures her place on the evacuation ship Atlas, learning the passenger list is a currency of favors and lies. POV: Sable. Emotional beat: ambition sharpened by desperation.

chapters.title: A Face She Burned
chapters.summary: A memory chapter: young Sable watching her sister Livia choose marriage over escape, and Sable choosing the courier's life in retaliation. POV: Sable (flashback). Emotional beat: the origin of her leaving.

chapters.title: The Boy Who Would Not Speak
chapters.summary: Back in the present, Tomas finally speaks—a single word, Sable's false name—which terrifies her more than any checkpoint. POV: Sable. Emotional beat: the child has made her real, and therefore vulnerable.

chapters.title: Occupier's Dinner
chapters.summary: To renew her transit papers, Sable dines with an occupation officer who may know exactly who she is; he lets her leave, which is worse. POV: Sable. Emotional beat: dread dressed as civility.

chapters.title: Letters to a Sister Who Reads Nothing
chapters.summary: Marta discovers Sable writes unsent letters to Livia each night; a tentative friendship forms over shared griefs. POV: Marta. Emotional beat: loneliness confessed at last.

chapters.title: The Manifest Changes
chapters.summary: Sable learns the Atlas has lost berths to military priority; her own passage is now conditional on delivering a final, dangerous dispatch inland. POV: Sable. Emotional beat: the price of survival made explicit.

chapters.title: Livia at the Gate
chapters.summary: Livia arrives at the safehouse, widowed and hunted, asking not for forgiveness but for a berth. POV: Livia. Emotional beat: old wounds reopened by necessity, not reconciliation.

chapters.title: Two Names, One Coat
chapters.summary: Sable and Livia forge documents together, their old sibling fluency returning in forgery, argument, and silence. POV: alternating. Emotional beat: love expressed through competence.

chapters.title: The Dispatch
chapters.summary: Sable delivers the final codes and discovers they contain the evacuation list itself—names to be saved, names to be abandoned, hers among the latter. POV: Sable. Emotional beat: betrayal by the state she served.

chapters.title: What Marta Cannot Carry
chapters.summary: Marta refuses a berth, choosing to stay with her bedridden mother; she asks Sable to take her locket instead. POV: Marta. Emotional beat: dignity in staying behind.

chapters.title: The Officer's Offer
chapters.summary: The occupation officer offers Sable a berth and safety in exchange for the names of other couriers. POV: Sable. Emotional beat: temptation framed as mercy.

chapters.title: Arithmetic at Midnight
chapters.summary: Sable calculates: one berth, three people who need it—Livia, Tomas, herself—and the arithmetic refuses every solution. POV: Sable. Emotional beat: the novel's moral fulcrum.

chapters.title: The Burning
chapters.summary: Sable burns the coded dispatches, erasing the list and her own name from the republic's last ledger. POV: Sable. Emotional beat: liberation disguised as treason.

chapters.title: Checkpoint at the Harbor Road
chapters.summary: The three travel to the docks; stopped at a final checkpoint, Livia claims Tomas as her son, using Sable's forged papers flawlessly. POV: Livia. Emotional beat: the sisters' trust, finally proven.

chapters.title: The Last Berth
chapters.summary: At the gangway, only one berth remains; Sable gives it to Tomas, telling him to remember her face—reversing the note that started everything. POV: Sable. Emotional beat: climax; grief and love in a single gesture.

chapters.title: The Atlas Departs
chapters.summary: Sable and Livia watch the ship pull away through the crowd, holding each other, hunted but no longer alone. POV: Sable. Emotional beat: devastation transformed into kinship.

chapters.title: The Country of the Staying
chapters.summary: The sisters go underground with Marta's network, learning that those who remain build something the departed cannot. POV: Marta. Emotional beat: quiet hope amid occupation.

chapters.title: A Letter That Arrives
chapters.summary: Years later, a letter from Tomas—now grown, safe abroad—reaches Sable; she finally signs her true name. POV: Sable. Emotional beat: resolution; identity chosen, not survived.
